91.s: He learned improvising while learning the instrument, hearing changes by ear, as with Red Allen.
91.q: And I was hearing improvisation on records and in some instances, in hearing musicians live, and having fooled around a little with the piano, I kind of could hear, you know, changes, chord structures, a little -- and this is very basic to improvisation, you know, to learn this, or at least be able…

91.t: Early improvising on "Old Fashioned Love" and Erroll Garner
91.s: Carter recalls improvising on Old Fashioned Love about 1921 and says Erroll Garner shows the mystery.
91.q: NO. No. It was ... Arthur Briggs was the trumpet player in Paris --but there was another -- could there be 2 Arthur Briggs? I never thought of this before but he was ... Gibbs! Arthur Dr. Gibbs, I think, yeah, a pianist.

259.t: Big Eye Louis, Buddy Christian and a recent carnival-day job
259.s: Vincent says he played with Big Eye Louis but did not know his father. He tells of a recent carnival job with a young sax player, and says Buddy Christian played house parties and learned chords by guiding other players' fingers.
259.ch: Banjo career, Armstrong and the Liberty Bell
259.q: Did you know his father? Oh, what you mean, chronically? Yeah. Yeah. No, I didn't know Big Eye Louis. I didn't know his daddy. Then I got another Big Eye Louis Robinson piano player. Just told about him, eh? Yeah. Yeah. He was good, but he used to say he played too long like a woman, you know. But…

432.t: Learning chords and playing like Benny Goodman and Lionel Hampton
432.s: He explains the chord lessons, ninth chords, and learning from visiting big bands.
432.q: Oh the trumpet. Yeah. See, where that story is, there's a garage there now. But what I mean, I used to play up on a TikTok up there with, see Clyde Kerr and William Houston had a band up there, and Poirier bought them uniforms and everything, and when I won all them contests and everything, well I…

1032.t: Learning by rote and interweaving in group music, from Cuba to Irish pubs
1032.s: Rowe reads a percussionist's account of oral learning; they compare it to early jazz bandstands and to ensemble folk sessions in Ireland.
1032.q: Yeah. That’s right on. I totally hear him, yeah that’s exactly what it is like. Yeah. I mean and that’s not, you know, that’s not far off from the early jazz traditions too right? You know getting up on the bandstand and if you suck you’re off. If you even get that opportunity.

156.t: Repertoire and the college's indifference to jazz
156.s: Tunes the band played, the college's bemused attitude, and learning harmony in Berrian Shute's music appreciation course.
156.q: Well we played all those standard things, “Muskrat Ramble” and “The Saints Go Marching In,” and “Black and Blue” and oh the blues of course and probably “Memphis Blues,” I can’t remember exactly. There was one we used to do all the time called “She Looks Like Helen Brown.” I’ve never heard of it…

656.t: Accordion trio, fake books and discovering alternate blues changes
656.s: In high school he learned changes by playing through fake books with an accordion trio, then worked out alternate chord substitutions at the piano.
656.q: Wow. I’d say sometime in high school. Maybe sophomore year, somewhere around there. There was a point where I was playing with an accordion trio. We were playing a lot of weddings and that kind of thing. The guy played chordovox, the organ type accordion, but before that regular accordion. And I…

108.t: Learning to improvise from chord symbols
108.s: With a reading background he gradually learns to relate guitar chord symbols to the harmony.
108.ch: Childhood and learning music in Philadelphia
108.q: It was rather strange, because I didn’t really understand it. They would put the chords down, and I wasn’t certain just how the chords should be interpreted. Many times I would be just playing chords in the rhythm of it [Wilder sings a chordal arpeggio] similar to the Arban studies that I had and…

92.t: Lionel Hampton's band visits; Prez played chords by ear
92.s: Hampton's first band came to hear them rehearse, and Collins learned that Prez knew no chord names yet ran intricate patterns by ear.
92.ch: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
92.q: rehearse, down to Woodside. And they stayed around for awhile, but it was quite an experience playing -- I learned a lot playing with Prez. Well, I mean I -- well, one thing, Prez didn't know chords, but he had an innate sense. He had an ear that was just terrific, you know. He would make an intro…

19.t: After-hours jam sessions; Frank Higgs makes him play I Got Rhythm in B-flat
19.s: Big-band players jam at his beer garden job; a tenor player forces him to play in B-flat, and he learns tunes and chord calls from horn players.
19.ch: Washington in the 1930s: big bands, lessons, first jobs
19.q: So there was all this music around, and I had to listen to it, and I was growing by leaps and bounds. And at this particular job where I was working, whenever these fellows got off from work... Then as now, whenever guys work in a big band, they never get enough of a chance to play, or never get to…
